summary: The bill caps the H-2A temporary agricultural worker program at 400,000 certified positions per fiscal year, excluding positions filled by union-represented workers, by amending the Immigration and Nationality Act.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to impose an annual cap on H-2A certifications. It contains no provisions altering federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgets.
The bill makes no changes to tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.
No provisions address health insurance, medical care delivery, or healthcare regulation.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The core purpose is to restrict the H-2A temporary agricultural worker program by capping certifications at 400,000 positions annually. This directly limits a legal immigration pathway for foreign farm labor, aligning with efforts to restrict immigration and protect domestic workers from foreign labor competition.
No references to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or armed forces policy.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, emissions, or conservation policy.
No changes to welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement benefits.
No provisions relate to schools, student aid, or education policy.
The legislation contains nothing on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No impact on sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal procedure.
The bill does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No fiscal measures affecting deficits, debt ceilings, or borrowing.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not address foreign assistance programs or international aid.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance provisions.
Nothing in the text concerns technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.

The bill protects domestic farmworkers by capping the H-2A program and explicitly exempts union-represented positions from the cap. This strengthens worker protections against wage suppression and gives preferential treatment to unionized agricultural labor, advancing union interests.
No provisions on religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination rules.
